Principle that legal burden of proof always remains on the prosecution is the most fundamental principle of our Criminal Jurisprudence and is much older than the Evidence Act, because it was the principle of common law administered by Apex Court of the Sub-Continent. It is, thus, elementary principle of criminal law that in all criminal cases the burden of proof lies upon the prosecution to bring the guilt home to the door of accused persons beyond any reasonable doubt. Proof beyond reasonable doubt means proof of an offence with the certainty of criminal law; the certainty is that offence is committed and that no other person but the accused person on the evidence committed offence. It is, also, to be borne in mind that vague hunches cannot take the place of Judicial evaluation. Presumption, conjectures and surmises cannot take the field of evidence. The conviction on the basis of shaky and unreliable evidence by witnesses would not be at all proper and legal.

This brings us to the factum of absconsion of convict-appellants Babul alias Jalil Howlader, Yusuf Howlader and Jafar Sarder and non-appealing convicts Chan Mia alias Arif Talukder and Jamal Talukder. Babul alias Jalil Howlader, Yusuf Howlader and Jafar Sardar on surrender presented criminal appeal along with other convict-appellants. Learned Counsel Mr Ziaul Hasan, representing convict-appellants, informed that Chan Mia alias Arif Talukder had been arrested by police and he is in jail. Jamal Talukder is in abscondence. Abscondence of an accused does not automatically amount to evidence of guilty mind and abscondence is equally consistent with innocence and guilt. Abscondence sometimes is an incriminating circumstance to the quilt of accused person but mere abscondence cannot always be a circumstance to lead to an inference of guilt of accused person. Sometimes, out of fear and self-respect and, .also, to avoid unnecessary harassment even an innocent person may remain in abscondence. Abscondence by itself is not conclusive either of guilt or of a guilty conscience. Of course, abscondence of the accused may sometimes furnish corroboration of the prosecution evidence.
